Why This Is Your Job Now
Clients judge an online store by the sales report.
Outside Our Control
  • Product
  • Price
  • Traffic
Ours
  • Information architecture
  • Product page template
  • Cart behaviour
  • Mobile speed
“Here’s how we’ll make sure this sells” is a different conversation, with different clients and different fees.

Design for Conversion
The Framework
20 points across 7 areas.
Simplify · Clarity → Beautify · Confidence → Amplify · Momentum
Simplify
  • Clear value proposition
  • Homepage focus
  • Descriptive product titles
  • Product descriptions that sell and inform
  • Easy-to-shop collections
  • Guided choices
  • Useful search
Beautify
  • Product photography and video
  • Product page structure
  • Perceived value
  • Reviews and social proof
  • Trust signals
  • Shipping and returns clarity
Amplify
  • Visible add to cart
  • Clear calls to action
  • An understandable cart
  • A smooth checkout
  • Worthwhile email capture
Across The Journey
  • Mobile experience
  • Site speed

Before You Touch The Design
Start with evidence, not opinions.
01
Funnel events
View item · add to cart · begin checkout · purchase
02
Site search tracking
The customer’s own words
03
Session recordings or heatmaps
E.g. Microsoft Clarity (free)
04
Landing pages
The product template is often the real homepage
Data tells you where to look. The 20 points tell you what to look for.

Amplify
Remove friction, catch the not-yet.
~70% Average Cart Abandonment (Baymard Institute)
  • Forced accounts · surprise costs
  • Too many fields · no autocomplete
  • No express payment
Trigger email capture on scroll, time or exit intent — not in the first two seconds

Across The Journey
Thumbs and milliseconds.
Thumb Zone
Primary actions in thumb reach · tap targets 24px minimum (WCAG 2.2), ~44px comfortable · test on a real phone, real connection
Core Web Vitals (Good)
≤2.5s
LCP
≤200ms
INP
≤0.1
CLS
Usual culprits: oversized hero (never lazy-load it, use fetchpriority=“high”) · app and script bloat · late-loading banners
